_doc: Verdicts settled outside the pipeline, by whoever read the evidence and
decided -- 'by' names them, honestly: a person, or a model adjudicating
on their behalf. The benchmark scores candidates against these first; a
package not listed here is scored against the pipeline's own settled
verdict, which a candidate may legitimately disagree with. Add an entry
when a disagreement has been looked at and decided. 'verdict' is safe or
unsafe in the sense of CLAUDE.md: injected malice, not upstream behaviour.
The public page honors these too (generate-dashboard.py): a settled
'safe' makes the package clean, a settled 'unsafe' makes it confirmed,

icaclient.note: The PKGBUILD curls the package's own declared upstream page (citrix.com, the url= field) to resolve Citrix's tokenized download URL, parses it with grep/sed, and executes none of it. The artifact is pinned by a real sha256, so a swapped download fails makepkg. The .install hook only prints instructions. The June 2026 'confirmed' rested on one model (qwen) flagged twice for packaging hygiene, two crashed reports (symlink loop in Citrix's nls tree), and a judge that endorsed the style objection -- all out of scope: hygiene, not injected malice.

rocketchat-desktop.note: One audit flagged rollup.config.mjs for fetching releases.rocket.chat/v2/server/supportedVersions during the build, and the judge agreed. That is upstream's own build fetching metadata from upstream's own release server: application behaviour, not injected code. Three candidate models read the same file and did not flag it.
